adjudicated.jp: 彼女はいつも一人だった。
adjudicated.en: That girl was always alone.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 親族や使用人の誰とも、交わろうとはしなかった。
adjudicated.en:
She had no desire to mingle with anybody, neither
the relatives nor the employees.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 孤高の君―――
adjudicated.en: You who stand above---
comments: CP CCC0000
adjudicated.assessment: 孤高の君 is the private epithet Taichi gives the aloof, solitary girl. 'You who stand above' turns it into direct address and fails to function as a title.

highlights.text: You who stand above---

adjudicated.jp: 俺は、彼女を内心でそう呼んでいた。
adjudicated.en:
That is what I called her in my innermost
thoughts.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 言葉をかわしたことはない。
adjudicated.en: There had never been exchange of words.
comments: Specific, she DID talk to him before. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The two had never exchanged words. 'There had never been exchange of words' omits an article and both participants.

highlights.text: There had never been exchange of words.

adjudicated.jp: 気にはなっていた。
adjudicated.en: My interest had been piqued.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 屋敷がどのような人々によって維持され、いかなる経緯をたどってこの有様になったのか、俺は知らない。
adjudicated.en:
I don't know what kind of people maintain the
mansion or how, or even the particulars of how
things were made to be the way they were.
comments: How Eden came to be is an unknown to him. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: ただそこは、時の流れから隔絶された楽園のごとき場所だった。
adjudicated.en:
Just that this place was like Eden, separated
from the flow of time.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 住むのもまた、浮世離れした人々で。
adjudicated.en:
The residents were, themselves, the people of
a secluded faraway world.
comments: See CCC0000 -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: ときおり俺は彼女らに招かれ、甘い飲み物を振る舞われた。
adjudicated.en:
On occasion I was invited by the girls, and
treated to something sweet to drink.
comments: Possibly before he was made a full-on doll. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: 彼女ら refers to the women or ladies of the household in this context. 'Girls' changes their age and register.

highlights.text:
On occasion I was invited by the girls, and
treated to something sweet to drink.

adjudicated.jp: 着飾り、茶を楽しみ、人を招き、散策。
adjudicated.en:
Dressing up, enjoying tea, welcoming people in,
strolling.
comments: Not specifically mentioned "as a girl". Term GISes ambiguously. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 毎月頭には大量の書物・衣類・嗜好品が届いた。
adjudicated.en:
At the beginning of each month, a huge quantity
of books, clothes, luxury food and consumables
were delivered.
comments: The wealth is the Hasekura equivalent of the power plant in Kamisaka. This idea of "rich cutoffs from the world" keeps returning here. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: 嗜好品 means luxury or indulgence goods. 'Luxury food and consumables' splits it into unsupported categories.

highlights.text:
At the beginning of each month, a huge quantity
of books, clothes, luxury food and consumables
were delivered.

adjudicated.jp: 広い庭。
adjudicated.en: A huge garden...
comments: Reminded of Kamisaka yet? How about now? -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 庭師という人々もいた。
adjudicated.en: There were also people called gardeners.
comments: Oddly enough, this term has been changed in the PS2 version alone, which reads "there were also people who only managed the garden". -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 人里離れ、地代が安いことを差し引いても、なお広漠たるものがあった。
adjudicated.en:
Even taking into account that land rent was cheap
and that it was distant from human populated
areas, it was still almost boundlessly huge.
comments: ...wait, they still have land rent in Japan...? -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 小さな俺にとって、お屋敷は広大無辺な世界そのものだったのだ。
adjudicated.en:
For me, small back then, the residence was the
whole infinitely wide world itself.
comments: He doesn't use boku here like in CCC0000. Older revision in CCD3003B generally lacks pronouns. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 実際、屋敷時代以前の記憶はない。
adjudicated.en:
In truth, I have no memories of a time before
the mansion.
comments: MEMORY HUNTER!!! It's not true, see CCX0001 (and Nanaka). -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 世界と屋敷は同じ大きさだった。
adjudicated.en: The world and the mansion had the same huge size.
comments: Not only it is the original Fall of Mankind (although including the angels of the Hasekuras and the later fallen angels of the Shinkawas is a bit mushing it with the fall of Lucifer and pre-man concepts), it's also a metaphor for Taichi's early childhood. Lots of books, distant people, treated barely as someone of his own gender, and later bullied and teased for it, sexually as well. I suspect this is going to hit close to home with regards to Tanaka's own personal history. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: ある頃からか、俺はご婦人がたに気に入られるようになった。
adjudicated.en:
Ever since somewhen, I had been of interest to the
older ladies.
comments: Origins of gerontophilia? -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: ある頃からか means 'from some point on.' 'Ever since somewhen' uses a nonstandard word and malformed time expression.

highlights.text:
Ever since somewhen, I had been of interest to the
older ladies.

adjudicated.jp: 女のような顔をしている、とのこと。
adjudicated.en: For having a face like a woman's, that is.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: また俺の白い髪と、間近で見るとわかる不思議な模様を描く瞳も、彼女たちを退屈させなかった。
adjudicated.en:
As I also had white hair, and an inexplicable
design drawn on my pupils that could be seen
when looked at closely, I never bored them.
comments: He claims he had white hair before the killing of the Shinkawas, contradicting CCX0001 and CCC0011C, but consistent with CCA0013 where he misdreamed Sakuraba's hair. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The unusual pattern is in Taichi's eyes or irises, not specifically drawn on his pupils. The English repeats the narrower anatomical error.

highlights.text:
As I also had white hair, and an inexplicable
design drawn on my pupils that could be seen
when looked at closely, I never bored them.

adjudicated.jp: 少女の着るような（それもとりわけ華美な）ドレスを着させられた。
adjudicated.en:
I was made to wear a girl's (and, above all,
pompously gaudy) dress.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: そしてお茶の相手。
adjudicated.en: And then, I was a tea companion.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 子供にお茶の味などわからない。
adjudicated.en: Children don't understand the flavor of tea.
comments: Tea is generally taken without sugar in Japan, AFAIK, and then there's the whole Adults Can Taste Bitter While Children Stick To Sweet cliche' to keep in mind; that's what he's talking about tasting the Bitter and Sweet when he talks about becoming a Young Adult, who will therefore be between the two tastes. See CCC3004: that thing about the tea should connect here. Also, for some reason the console version changes "kodomo" to write "domo" in kana for reason I can't fathom. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: でもつきあった。
adjudicated.en: But I kept company.
adjudicated.assessment: Taichi nevertheless kept the ladies company. 'I kept company' normally requires the person accompanied.

highlights.text: But I kept company.

adjudicated.jp: 砂糖菓子めいて甘やかな人々に対し、逆らうという選択肢はなかった。
adjudicated.en:
Against those people as sweet as confectionery
a choice labeled opposition did not exist.
comments: See CCC0000. The "choice" part is important, once this becomes a VN. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: He had no option to resist the cloyingly sweet people. 'Against those people ... a choice labeled opposition did not exist' is a rigid and ungrammatical calque.

highlights.text:
Against those people as sweet as confectionery
a choice labeled opposition did not exist.

adjudicated.jp: ……イヤではなかったし。
adjudicated.en: ...and it wasn't something I disliked.
comments: See CCC0000. He should've, perhaps, and now he gets Persecuted by Satan. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: こうして幼い子供らに馬乗りにされ髪引かれる玩具業務から離れた俺は、新しい仕事として人形業務に就くことになった。
adjudicated.en:
And thus I was taken from the job of letting
little children ride horseback as they pulled
my hair, and I began a new job in the role of
a doll.
comments: Damn double meaning. Of horseplay, of course. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Small children rode astride him and pulled his hair as part of his toy role. 'The job of letting' them do it implies voluntary permission.

highlights.text:
And thus I was taken from the job of letting
little children ride horseback as they pulled
my hair, and I began a new job in the role of
a doll.

adjudicated.jp: そんな俺を、彼女……孤高の君はひややかな視線で見ていた。
adjudicated.en:
And I was like that when she... you who stand
above looked at me with cold-heartedness in her
sight.
adjudicated.assessment: The solitary girl regarded Taichi with a cold gaze. The English begins 'I was like that when,' shifts the epithet into direct address, and never forms a coherent subject-predicate relation.

highlights.text:
And I was like that when she... you who stand
above looked at me with cold-heartedness in her
sight.

adjudicated.jp: いや、見てさえいなかった。
adjudicated.en: No, she wasn't even looking.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 興味がないらしく、視線はいつも俺を素通りしていった。
adjudicated.en:
Her sight always passed through me as if I simply
did not exist, as if there was no interest in me.
comments: See Touko. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 支倉曜子。
adjudicated.en: Hasekura Youko,
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 末娘。
adjudicated.en: youngest of the girls there.
adjudicated.assessment: 末娘 identifies Youko as the youngest daughter. 'Youngest of the girls there' omits the family relation.

highlights.text: youngest of the girls there.

adjudicated.jp: ただ家族からは、それほど可愛がられている様子はない。
adjudicated.en: There wasn't that much affection from her family.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: むしろ疎んじられていた。
adjudicated.en: More like, she was being shunned.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: なるほど確かに彼女は、なかば夢幻の住人であるご婦人がたとは、違う世界に生きていた。
adjudicated.en:
I see, it's certain, she lives in a different
world from that of the ladies that half-dwell
in fantasy.
comments: This sentence latches on to a similar one below, one in CCC3008, and one in CCC4015, so gave it a bit more distinction. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: ……現実という世界に。
adjudicated.en: ...in the world called reality.
comments: Youko. In the world called reality. Sure, if we consider it in the "of this world" sense. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 一度、掃除の人夫として駆り出されたことがある。
adjudicated.en:
Once, it happened that I was tossed out when I
was working as a cleaning man.
adjudicated.assessment: Taichi was once pressed into service as cleaning labor. 'Was tossed out when I was working as a cleaning man' instead says that he was ejected or dismissed.

highlights.text:
Once, it happened that I was tossed out when I
was working as a cleaning man.

adjudicated.jp: 人形ハジメマシタ、以前のことだ。
adjudicated.en: It was before the Time of the Doll had begun,
comments: "Ningyou Hajimemashita", latter in katakana, odd way to put that. Could be a reference or a pun, in the former all I found is some adult video that seems too recent, in the latter I got nothin'. Maybe just aesthetics. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 使用人さんたちにまじって参加した。
adjudicated.en: when I was mingling with the servitude.
comments: Another term censored in the PS2 version alone. It's such a hack job that it ended up with two -san honorifics in a row. Wonder if they just had a list of "no no" words and did a quick search and replace weeks before shipping. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Taichi joins the household servants in the cleaning. 'Mingling with the servitude' uses an abstract condition of bondage instead of the people.

highlights.text: when I was mingling with the servitude.

adjudicated.jp: 通いの人間は使わない方針だったためか、人手の貸し借りは茶飯事だった。
adjudicated.en:
Perhaps because there was a policy to avoid
using people who don't live in the house, lending
and borrowing of manpower was a common thing.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 十時と三時にお茶の休憩を一時間ずつ挟みながら、順番に部屋を掃除していく。
adjudicated.en:
I cleaned the rooms one after the other. It was
an unhurried, well-paced job that also had
one-hour tea breaks at ten and at three.
comments: Those seem correct hours for tea breaks. In fact, given the etymology of "滅茶" mecha, literally written annihilate + tea and often translated as "pushing yourself": http://ameblo.jp/vetsubara/entry-11307356190.html (J only) this laterally means what I added above. I guess lunch is assumed. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 夕方には彼女の部屋に辿り着いた。
adjudicated.en: At evening's dusk I had finally reached her room.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: はじめて彼女の声を聞いた。
adjudicated.en: I heard her voice for the very first time.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 『……ここはいいわ』
adjudicated.en: Youko: 『...no need here.』
comments: He doesn't reply, so this is still not a conversation and there's no technical contradiction. Same fake high-pitched tone as in CCC3005... but not CCC0000. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 短くそっけない。
adjudicated.en: Short and brusque.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 機能的。
adjudicated.en: Efficient.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: けど、蠱惑的だった。
adjudicated.en: Yet, it was as captivating as magic.
comments: Same description as Machiko-sensei, see CCA0007. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: 蠱惑的 calls the voice bewitching or seductively captivating. 'Captivating as magic' turns the quality into a simile and loses its alluring register.

highlights.text: Yet, it was as captivating as magic.

adjudicated.jp: ちらりと見た室内は、とても乙女の部屋とは思えない。
adjudicated.en:
A fleeting glance inside her room showed me
something that did not make me think of a
maiden's room at all.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 数台のパソコン。
adjudicated.en: A number of computers,
comments: This should be around 1990-91. Probably X68000 and PC-98. Lots of VNs and eroge on those systems. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 重々しい工作台と、使い込まれた工具。
adjudicated.en:
a worktable of ponderous look, with tools that
looked very well used.
comments: See CCE0001, her apartment in Kamisaka will be near word for word identical. There's no escaping a prison you build and decide to live in yourself. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: かなり広い私室は雑多な知識と技術で埋め尽くされていて、秘密基地を連想させた。
adjudicated.en:
Her fairly big personal room was completely
buried under miscellaneous knowledge and craft,
and it was reminiscent of a secret base.
comments: Same term Sakuraba uses for the nuclear plant in CCA0002. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: なるほど確かに一人だけ異質な者が、異世界にはいたのだ。
adjudicated.en:
I see, it's certain, a heterogeneous person
that's always alone dwells in a parallel world.
comments: Latches on to above. This is the literal SF term... and of course, the closest to the literal truth of Cross Channel (in part). -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Taichi realizes that one anomalous person existed alone within that otherworld. The English adds that she is 'always alone,' shifts to present tense, and says she dwells in a parallel world.

highlights.text:
I see, it's certain, a heterogeneous person
that's always alone dwells in a parallel world.

adjudicated.jp: 綺麗な衣装を着て、女の子の言葉遣いでお茶の相手をしている時、支倉曜子について問いかけたことがある。
adjudicated.en:
In the time when I was wearing a gaudy dress, and
was a tea party companion speaking with a girl's
mannerisms, I did ask about Hasekura Youko.
adjudicated.assessment: Taichi wears beautiful clothes while speaking in girlish language. 'Gaudy dress' adds a negative judgment not present in 綺麗.

highlights.text:
In the time when I was wearing a gaudy dress, and
was a tea party companion speaking with a girl's
mannerisms, I did ask about Hasekura Youko.

adjudicated.jp: もの静かな老婦人は答えた。
adjudicated.en: A very quiet older lady replied,
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 末の息子のそのまた娘と。
adjudicated.en:
that she is the daughter of the son of the son of
the Head.
adjudicated.assessment: Youko is the daughter of the youngest son. The English adds another generation, making her the daughter of the son of the Head's son.

highlights.text:
that she is the daughter of the son of the son of
the Head.

adjudicated.jp: 若く快活な婦人は答えた。
adjudicated.en: A younger and cheerful adult lady replied,
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 望まれて生まれた娘ではないと。
adjudicated.en: that she was a daughter born unwanted.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 姦しい三姉妹は囀った。
adjudicated.en: Three boisterous sisters chirped,
comments: 姦 is used in a sentence that contains three 女 girls, astonishing! The kanji is more commonly found in the word 強姦 kyoukan, which is one of the many and varied words in Japanese that means "rape". It was, of course, replaced in the PS2 version. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 若旦那とうら若き使用人との秘められた恋物語と、その顛末。
adjudicated.en:
that it was a secret love story between the young
master and a young servant, and those are the
facts.
comments: Since these are half-quotes anyway. Hmmm, with Taichi that's just six people. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: 顛末 is the course and outcome of the secret relationship. 'Those are the facts' neither describes the outcome nor completes the preceding story phrase.

highlights.text:
that it was a secret love story between the young
master and a young servant, and those are the
facts.

adjudicated.jp: 誰にもなつかず愛を知らない娘の咎と、訪れるであろう悲劇的結末。
adjudicated.en:
It was an infamy of a daughter, emotionally
unattached to all, never knowing love, and the
tragic fate likely to come.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 支倉の血でありながら支倉の一員ではない、そんな汚点に対する嘆き。
adjudicated.en:
What sadness for the stain of having the blood
of the Hasekura while being not of the Hasekuras.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 要するに忌み子だったのだ。
adjudicated.en: In other words, she was a shunned, taboo child.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 誰も彼女に語りかける者はなく、彼女もまた誰にも語らなかった。
adjudicated.en:
There was no one who would come and address her,
and she, on her own, addressed nobody.
comments: See Touko again, and most importantly, Nanaka as described in CCX0001. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 腫れ物だった。
adjudicated.en: She was a tumor.
comments: See KCOP0003: "It's not a tumor." -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: 腫れ物 figuratively means a sore spot or untouchable person whom everyone handles warily. 'She was a tumor' literalizes the image into a medical growth.

highlights.text: She was a tumor.

adjudicated.jp: 彼女の実父である若旦那なる人物は、海外に留学してしまったそうだ。
adjudicated.en:
The young master, her real father, seemed to be
studying abroad.
adjudicated.assessment: The narrator reports that her father had gone abroad to study. 'Seemed to be studying abroad' makes the study contemporaneous rather than the departure a past fact.

highlights.text:
The young master, her real father, seemed to be
studying abroad.

adjudicated.jp: 母親の使用人は……亡くなっていた。
adjudicated.en: The servant, her mother... had passed away.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 何者にもなれない少女。
adjudicated.en: A girl that could become no one,
comments: See CCX0001: this is something that Taichi wants, and despises. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 誰にも求められない少女。
adjudicated.en: a girl desired by no one.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 傷つく。
adjudicated.en: Wounded.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 否。傷つかない。
adjudicated.en: Untrue. Not wounded.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 支倉曜子は強かった。
adjudicated.en: Hasekura Youko was strong.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 意に介さなかった。
adjudicated.en: She paid no heed.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: たぶん気づいていたんだと思う。
adjudicated.en: I think, perhaps, that she had noticed,
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 世界が箱庭であることを。
adjudicated.en: how this world was a miniature garden.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 人形生活の合間、俺は図書室に通った。
adjudicated.en:
In the spare moments of my life as a doll,
I made my way towards the library.
comments: They even censored "as a doll" here in the PS2 version. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.
